title: TSMC Demands Operational Control of Musk Terafab Site in Project Clash

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Chief Executive Officer C.C. Wei announced that TSMC will only participate in Elon Musk's Texas semiconductor venture if the foundry is granted full governing authority over the plants. The Taiwanese chipmaker is currently weighing a new Texas campus that would add tens of billions of dollars to its existing $265B investment in Arizona, provided the company manages the resulting facilities.

The demand creates a standoff with Musk, who previously stated his businesses would independently build and operate the 'Terafab' complex, limiting TSMC to a potential sublease of the site. The project aims for 1 TW of annual compute production and a cycle of 10 chip designs per year to serve Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI. Intel has already partnered with the Texas project, providing its 14A process technology to support Musk's hardware requirements.

selectedTweets.text:
Elon, this really doesn’t make sense… Why would equipment makers build custom tools specifically for Terafab? They can simply keep selling the tools they already make to Intel, TSMC, and Samsung. Why would they spend extra on R&D to develop tools exclusively for Terafab?

If Terafab really wants equipment makers to build these custom tools, it’ll have to put up an enormous amount of money. The number of tools required and the amount you’d have to spend on them would be on a completely different scale from manufacturing EVs or rockets.

“I still have a lot to learn about chip making. Gotta start somewhere. I didn’t know how to make cars or rockets. The (chip) equipment’s not very customized, it’s all coming from the same vendors.
